email.body1:
Tim, saw Campfire raised its $65M Series B and acquired Cover 4 PM, all on the back of 10x revenue growth.

Growing commercial that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new reps ramp, and that is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Campfire off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Tim, quick follow-up for Campfire.

After a raise like that, board expectations on pipeline tend to jump faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they actually need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Campfire needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Tim, last bit of proof for Campfire.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Campfire's reply rate likely compares to other recently funded startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Tim, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling commercial pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem. Timing matters right after a raise, and the fundraise-to-hiring stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your growth motion? I will tailor it to Campfire either way.
